body_markdown:
Private models can handle many routine agent tasks, depending on workload and configuration. When a task needs Claude, send it through the same gateway, on the same keys, under the same admin controls.


Most of the agent work I see in customer labs doesn’t need a frontier model. Summarizing an alert or extracting invoice fields is work a private model on Nutanix Enterprise AI handles, and the data never leaves the building. In our lab experience, many routine agent tasks can be handled by private models, while selected complex reasoning and coding tasks may benefit from frontier models. Routine agent work runs on private models through OpenAI-compatible tools like OpenCode, covered in[Configure OpenCode v2 to Use Your Approved Models Through Nutanix Agent Gateway](https://www.nutanix.dev/2026/10/28/configure-opencode-v2-to-use-your-approved-models-through-nutanix-agent-gateway/) . Selected complex reasoning and coding work is where teams want Claude through Claude Code.


A developer using a personal Anthropic key outside organizational controls may create an unmanaged AI access path. Organizations can configure Claude Code to use a Nutanix Agent Gateway endpoint and apply a common gateway and policy workflow. Logging, audit behavior, and available controls depend on the provider, release, and configuration.


## Nutanix Agent Gateway and Claude Code


Nutanix Agent Gateway is the unified endpoint layer in Nutanix Enterprise AI (NAI). A unified endpoint gives clients one address for one or more models, either local endpoints served on NAI or models from external providers such as Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, GCP Vertex AI and OpenAI. It can spread traffic across its models by load balance weights or a fallback order. Clients authenticate with API client keys that you create and attach to specific unified endpoints.


NAI 2.8 added Messages API support: unified endpoints can now serve the Anthropic Messages API spec for Anthropic provider APIs, as a Messages task type. That’s the piece Claude Code needs. It sends Anthropic Messages requests to POST /v1/messages (or the Bedrock and Vertex native formats), and OpenAI Chat Completions is not a supported format for it.


Claude Code has first-class gateway support: set a base URL and a credential, and every model request goes to your gateway instead of Anthropic. Managed settings let an admin pin that configuration on every machine. Claude Desktop doesn’t read that configuration; it uses its own gateway setup (inferenceProvider: gateway), documented at[claude.com/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/gateway](https://claude.com/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/gateway) .


For the upstream, the gateway holds an Anthropic API key as a third-party credential. My lab uses a personal key; For production deployments, organizations should evaluate whether an organization-managed provider credential is appropriate for their billing, access, retention, and contractual requirements.


## Prerequisites


- NAI 2.8 with an Agent Gateway license applied.
- Claude Code v2.1.285 or later on managed machines (needed for allowedProviders).
- An Anthropic API key scoped to a workspace, with access to the Claude models you plan to offer. A Console key scoped to the whole organization needs an anthropic-workspace-id header on every request, which the NAI credential has no field for.
- A way to push files to developer machines: MDM, configuration management, or a golden image.


## Configure the gateway


1. In NAI, go to Settings, Third Party Credentials, click Add Credential, set Platform to Anthropic and paste your Anthropic API key in the API Key field.
2. Go to Providers, click Add Provider, set Platform to Anthropic and select that credential.
3. Go to API Client Keys and create a key for each developer or team. Per-user keys make usage attributable, and offboarding becomes one Deactivate or Delete on that key.
4. Go to Unified Endpoints and click Create Unified Endpoint. Set Task Type to Messages, which the guide limits to providers or endpoints built on Anthropic models that support messages ingress.
5. Click Add Model, select Provider, then select the Type as Provider. From the Provider dropdown, select the Anthropic provider, pick the model and enter its exact name in Model Name.
6. On the Configuration tab, select an API key from the API Client Keys dropdown, review the summary and click Create.


Clients address a unified endpoint by its Endpoint Name, not by the upstream model ID: the request’s model field carries the endpoint name and the gateway maps it to the model behind it. Plan one unified endpoint per Claude model you offer, and map each one to its model ID in Claude Code with modelOverrides, shown below.


Fig 01. Unified endpoint with NAI API key attached for “frontier 20”


## Smoke test from a developer machine


*Example configuration: These commands and settings are illustrative and were tested only in the stated environment. Validate them in a nonproduction environment before deploymen* t.”


Prove the path before touching managed settings.


```text
export NAI_FQDN="nai.example.com"   # your gateway FQDN
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="https://${NAI_FQDN}/enterpriseai/gateway"
export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="<your NAI API client key>"


curl -sS -w '\n%{http_code}\n' -X POST "$ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL/v1/messages" \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN" \
-H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \
-H "content-type: application/json" \
-d '{"model":"<UNIFIED_ENDPOINT_NAME>","max_tokens":64,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say ok"}]}'
```


The base URL stops at` /enterpriseai/gateway` ; Claude Code appends` /v1/messages` . The gateway reads the key from` Authorization: Bearer` , so use` ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` . Sent as` x-api-key` , the key is ignored and the gateway answers API key is not provided. A` 401` reading failed to validate API Key against multi-endpoint types means the model value doesn’t match a unified endpoint the key is attached to.


A` 200` means the path works with your NAI API Key. Then run claude, open` /status` , and check two lines: Anthropic base URL should show the gateway, and Auth token should name` ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` . A Login method line naming a claude.ai account means the credential didn’t take.


Exports last only for that shell. Once the test passes, move the variables into the env block of` ~/.claude/settings.json` and chmod` 600` the file, or Claude Code falls back to the claude.ai login on the next start without saying so. For a fleet, use managed settings instead. Use an organization-approved secret-management method where available; file permissions alone may not satisfy local security requirements.


```text
{
"env": {
"ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "https://nai.example.com/enterpriseai/gateway",
"ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN": "<your NAI API client key>"
},
"modelOverrides": {
"claude-sonnet-5-5": "<SONNET_ENDPOINT_NAME>"
}
}
```


## Lock Claude Code to the gateway with managed settings


Managed settings sit above user, project and command-line settings, and users can’t override them, apart from a few security settings where a stricter value from a lower level still applies. Drop this file in the system directory for each OS:


- Linux and WSL:` /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json`
- macOS:` /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/managed-settings.json` , or the` com.anthropic.claudecode` managed preferences domain through MDM
- Windows:` C:\\Program Files\\ClaudeCode\\managed-settings.json`


**Claude Documentation:**


- Claude managed settings


- [Local settings](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings)
- [Server settings](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings)


```text
{
"allowedProviders": ["customEndpoint"],
"apiKeyHelper": "/usr/local/bin/nai-gateway-key",
"skipWebFetchPreflight": true,
"modelOverrides": {
"claude-opus-5-5": "<OPUS_ENDPOINT_NAME>",
"claude-sonnet-5-5": "<SONNET_ENDPOINT_NAME>",
"claude-haiku-5-5": "<HAIKU_ENDPOINT_NAME>"
},
"env": {
"ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "https://nai.example.com/enterpriseai/gateway",
"CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC": "1"
}
}
```


- **allowedProviders:** \[“customEndpoint”\], with the base URL pinned in the same file’s env block, makes the gateway the configured destination for supported Claude Code model traffic.The documented managed-settings configuration is intended to restrict supported Claude Code model traffic to the configured endpoint; validate enforcement for the applicable version. Claude Code refuses a session pointed anywhere else, including Anthropic directly or a developer’s own proxy.
- **modelOverrides** maps each Anthropic model ID to the unified endpoint name that serves it. Claude Code still treats the session as Sonnet 5.5, with that model’s context window and capabilities, and sends the endpoint name to the gateway. Pinning the endpoint name in ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL also routes, but Claude Code doesn’t recognize the name, warns that it isn’t recognized, and assumes a 200K context window. /model switches between the three endpoints as usual.


Fig 02. Using modelOverrides to provide multiple models in` /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json`


- **apiKeyHelper** fetches the credential at runtime and sends it in both the Authorization and x-api-key headers; the gateway reads the Bearer one and accepts the request with both present.


***** Isolated Networks or Flow Network Security *****


` CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` and **skipWebFetchPreflight** matter on a fenced network: without the second, the WebFetch tool still runs a domain safety check against api.anthropic.com. Some Claude Code functions, such as availability checks and Fast mode, may require separate network access depending on the version and configuration. Validate required allowlists in the target environment.


If the gateway returns 400 errors naming unrecognized fields or beta values, add` "CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS": "1"` to env. Claude Code streams responses and sends` anthropic-beta` and` anthropic-version` headers, which the gateway should forward unchanged. In my environment having a coding session through the gateway, streaming, tool calls and file edits all work without that flag.


Fig 03. Claude code status menu. Settings viewed from the /status command.


## Tools through the same gateway


Model Context Protocol (MCP) is GA in NAI 2.8, and the gateway presents its MCP servers through a single` /mcp` interface with RBAC on which clients reach which tools. Two settings hold Claude Code to it.` allowManagedMcpServersOnly` can only be set in managed settings;` allowedMcpServers` can live in any settings file, and the lock makes the managed copy the only one that counts.


```text
{
"allowManagedMcpServersOnly": true,
"allowedMcpServers": [
{ "serverUrl": "https://nai.example.com/enterpriseai/gateway/mcp*" }
]
}
```


With the lock on (Claude Code v2.1.273 or later), a user’s own settings can’t widen the list, and once it holds a` serverUrl` entry every remote server has to match one. The gateway’s MCP interface takes the same API client key as a Bearer header.


## Wrap-up


Nutanix Agent Gateway can provide access to selected private and external model endpoints. Private models on NAI carry the bulk of the agent work through OpenAI-compatible tools. Claude Code carries the hard 20% through the same Nutanix Agent Gateway, on per-user keys you can deactivate, pinned by managed settings so it can’t wander off to a personal account.
